text: Jack and his mother had no money, only one cow. (Literally: "an animal that says 'moo'.") His mother said: "Take the cow, sell it, and bring the money back." On the road, an old man he'd never seen said: "Give me your cow, and I'll give you five magic beans." (Literally: "five little round things never seen before.") Jack went home. His mother was furious and threw the beans out of the window. That night, a plant came up out of the beans. It grew and grew, far up into the sky. Jack climbed up. At the top there was a huge house. In the house lived a giant (literally: "a really big person"). He had lots of gold. While the giant slept, Jack took his gold and hurried down. The giant woke up, saw Jack, and came down the plant after him! Jack broke the plant with a tool (an axe). The plant and the giant came crashing down, and the giant died. Jack and his mother had plenty of money and lived happily (literally: "lived very well").

blind.whole: Jiékè and his mother are poor and own only one animal, which the text calls "mōu" (a cow). The mother sends him to sell it, but on the road he gives it to an unknown old man for five small round things that nobody has seen before. His mother is very angry and throws them out of the window. During the night a plant grows from them and reaches the sky. Jiékè climbs it and finds a huge house at the top where a giant lives who has a lot of money. While the giant sleeps, Jiékè takes his money and hurries down. The giant wakes up and climbs down after him, but Jiékè breaks the plant with a tool. The plant and the giant fall to the ground and the giant dies. Jiékè and his mother are rich and live well.
blind.unsure: S1, S17, S18, S25 (jīn): the gloss says money, but the word can also mean gold. Either way it is wealth, so the reading hardly changes. S2: 'jiào "mōu"-de dòng-wù' can be 'an animal called mōu' or 'an animal that cries mōu'. I take both to mean a cow because of the sound. S3: 'gěi rén, dé jīn huí-lái' literally says give it to people, get money and come back. I read that as 'sell it'. S6/S12: 'xiǎo yuán dōng-xi' only says small round things. I call them seeds only because a plant grows out of them in S12. S9, S10, S11 (tā): I read tā as 'she', the mother, because S9 is about her. S11: I read 'kàn wài-miàn-de kǒu' (the opening for looking outside) as a window, and 'ná-chū-qù' as putting or throwing them out. S12: 'yuè-de shí-jiān' could be 'the moon's time', meaning night (my reading), or 'in a month's time', since yuè means both moon and month. S13: the gloss gives tiān-shàng as 'day-up'. I read tiān as sky, so the plant 'reached the sky'. S21: 'zài Jiékè hòu-miàn' may mean the giant was physically behind Jiékè, or that he came down after him. S22: 'zuò-huài' only says 'made it broken'. The text does not say how, so 'cut down' is my guess. S23: 'dào dì-shàng' literally means arrived on the ground (the gloss says floor). I read it as falling.

notes: Translated by hand following the translate skill (whole dictionary, no lesson), 2026-10-22. kb_memory returns the book's own Hao-shuo-de of this story (lesson none); its sentences were reused where they say the English and named in each source, and changed where they lose something: bàba-māma (parents) became māma (mother); the book's kǒu wài-miàn lost the window, so the form of 窗户 is used; the book's kuài xià-qù le became kuài-de xià-qù le, since kuài + verb + le is how about to is said (kb_lookup hurry points to about-to); Zài lù-shàng at the front became a place after the doer. Not said, by choice: "crashing" (only fell to the ground); throwing is weaker (not wanting, then taking out, the dictionary's form of 扔). Pitfalls met: "Yuè-de shí-jiān, yī-ge zhíwù …" with the comma reads only as calling out to the night in all 500 readings (and "Zài yuè-de shí-jiān, …" reads zài as a verb, also a call); without the comma the time reading is the first (time-first's rule Time S). The when-clause "Zhè-ge rén shuìjiào-de shí-jiān, …" also reads first as a call; the meant reading is number 213 of 238. "Tā-men huó-de hěn hǎo" reads first as "what they live is very good" (verb-de-thing); verb-de-how is reading 4. kb_lookup "cow" gives zhēn hǎo (from 牛's slang sense awesome) as a gloss-tier row: misleading. Glossary proposal: giant -> zhēn dà-de rén: no word, the test set's own literal, 3 words, then zhè-ge rén.
